target.title: fix(agents): bound GitHub release API response read in tools-manager
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `getLatestVersion` function in the agent tools-manager calls `response.json()` with no size limit against the GitHub releases API. While GitHub release JSON responses are typically ~500 bytes, the call has no guard against an oversized or malicious response.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `await response.json()` with a content-length pre-check plus `readResponseWithLimit(response, 64 * 1024)` and explicit `JSON.parse`. The content-length guard mirrors the bounded `downloadFile` pattern already present in the same file (line 186+). The imported `readResponseWithLimit` is the same helper used across the codebase for capped HTTP response reads.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The GitHub release version check now has the same bounded-read defense that the download path already applies.

## Evidence

Focused test proof:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

All 8 existing tests pass unchanged. Two new tests cover: declared content-length exceeding the 64KB cap is rejected before reading (body cancelled, guarded fetch released), and an oversized body stream without content-length is cancelled by the stream reader on overflow.

The same-file `downloadFile` function already applies content-length + per-chunk size guards; this change extends the same bounded-read discipline to the release metadata fetch.

AI-assisted. Real behavior proof collected by human.
